description: Real vs synthetic CSR comparison for EAMENA ley-line null FPR calibration

real_eamena_subset.interpretation: LEY_LINE_SIGNAL is a FALSE POSITIVE driven by spatial clustering (Clark-Evans R=0.37, z=-15.3). Archaeological sites cluster along environmental gradients (water, soil, trade routes), producing more collinear triples than naive CSR expects. This is NOT evidence of intentional ley-line geometry. The null model must be an inhomogeneous Poisson (Cox) process conditioned on covariates.

conclusion: FPR calibration on synthetic CSR data is clean: NO_SIGNAL verdict matches ground truth. However, on real EAMENA data, the naive CSR null produces a false positive LEY_LINE_SIGNAL because real archaeology is inhomogeneously clustered. A Cox process null (conditioned on environmental covariates) is needed for honest evaluation of real data. The synthetic CSR benchmark remains the correct FPR calibration tool.
